note: Lifted semantic model, Meridian (transport) side. Home-grown, no standard vocabulary. Each concept carries a bespoke label, synonyms, a shallow kind, a gloss, a canonical example, the ad-hoc reference entry the agent bound it to (ref; null = a native concept with no shared category), structural relations, and instances. A live side volunteers gloss/example; an inert side exposes only label, kind, relations, and instances, so its meaning must be reconstructed with no standard to lean on.

concepts.label: circuit
concepts.gloss: a provisioned transport circuit carrying a client end to end across the optical core; the underlay an external service rides
concepts.example: circuit CIR-7 from the NY hand-off to the Frankfurt hand-off

concepts.label: hand-off
concepts.gloss: the physical demarcation where a circuit presents to the client equipment
concepts.example: the NY hand-off port where CIR-7 meets the customer router

concepts.label: rate
concepts.gloss: the committed client payload rate the circuit guarantees end to end — not the bearer's line rate

concepts.label: latency
concepts.gloss: the one-way propagation delay of the circuit, a measured number of milliseconds set by path length
concepts.example: 7.2 ms one-way on CIR-7's primary path

concepts.label: protection
concepts.gloss: protection of the circuit against a failure of the transport path — a fiber cut or bearer loss — by switching to a diverse path
concepts.example: CIR-7 protected 1+1 against a cut on the primary fiber

concepts.label: grade
concepts.gloss: the transport quality grade of a circuit — its physical protection and restoration class
concepts.example: CIR-7 is a platinum-grade circuit (dual-path protected)

concepts.label: bearer
concepts.gloss: the physical optical bearer (a wavelength on a fiber) on which circuits are carried — a transport-internal object with no client-facing meaning
concepts.example: the 193.1 THz wavelength on the NY-FRA span carrying CIR-7
